about.text: To get a proposed constitutional amendment on the Ohio ballot, petitioners must submit their amendment, a summary of their amendment, and one thousand qualified supporting signatures to the Ohio Attorney General. The Ohio Attorney General must then determine if the summary is a fair and truthful statement of the proposed amendment and, if so, certify the summary.

events.description: OPINION and JUDGMENT filed : The district court’s order is REVERSED and Plaintiffs’ motion for preliminary injunctive relief is GRANTED. David Yost is ORDERED to send Plaintiffs’ proposed amendment and the most recent summary to the ballot board for the next phase of the proposed constitutional-amendment process. Plaintiffs’ motion for an injunction pending appeal [7159370-2] is DENIED AS MOOT. Mandate to issue. Decision for publication. Karen Nelson Moore (AUTHORING), John K. Bush (DISSENTING), and Andre B. Mathis, Circuit Judges.
